overview.text: The Jararaca is a highly venomous pit viper of south-eastern South America and a major cause of snakebites there. A blood-pressure medicine was developed from a substance found in its venom.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Slender; up to 160 cm, but usually much shorter.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The Atlantic Forest of southern and south-eastern Brazil, north-eastern Paraguay and Misiones in Argentina.

habitat.text: Mainly dense coastal tropical forest, also thickets, savanna, highland forest and farmland.

behaviour.text: Hunts mostly at night as a well-camouflaged ambush predator and hides in leaves by day; less active in cold months.
